question: Should ClawHub adopt a declared skill capability manifest now, and if so which schema, rollout, and authority model should it use?
rationale: The implementation shape is plausible, but the RFC intentionally leaves policy-sensitive choices open: advisory versus required rollout, field granularity, alignment with operator specs, legacy handling, and whether declarations are author-only or verified by ClawSweeper/ClawHub.

options.title: Adopt advisory manifest first
options.body: Add optional capability fields for new submissions, surface declared-vs-observed mismatches in review, and defer enforcement until the schema settles.

options.title: Coordinate with scanner RFC first
options.body: Keep this issue open but block implementation until the cross-asset review pipeline defines the observed-signal side of the diff.

options.title: Defer manifest schema
options.body: Continue with env/dependency declarations and manual security review until maintainers are ready to own a durable skill capability contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt advisory manifest first
recommendation.body: Add optional capability fields for new submissions, surface declared-vs-observed mismatches in review, and defer enforcement until the schema settles.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS and current-main provenance point to this handle for the schema/security-review surface where the decision would land.
